title: Quant Research Workbench
summary: A Python research workflow for testing how intraday futures ideas hold up under costs, fill uncertainty, and account rules.
question: How sensitive is a promising backtest to the fills and costs it assumes?

figure.alt: Bar chart comparing simulated lifecycle expectancy under baseline costs, added costs, and worse fills.
figure.caption: Execution stress in a simulated account lifecycle. The chart comes from the public workbench.

sections.title: What I built
sections.text: I assembled a research workflow around a fixed historical benchmark, later evaluation windows, and checks that isolate the effect of changing a policy or assumption. The public workbench includes trade summaries, bootstrap intervals, lifecycle simulations, and reports that can be rebuilt from the included artifacts.

sections.title: What the analysis showed
sections.text: In the published stress scenarios, a small added cost had less impact than degrading fills across the simulated trade stream. That made execution quality a priority for subsequent evaluation. The result depends on the historical trade sample and how the fill degradation was modeled.

sections.title: What the evidence covers
sections.text: The public release documents historical analysis and simulation. Real-world fill behavior and live profitability would require separate evidence.
